correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs. For n=k^2-d with k>=d+1, the Barmak--Minian minimum-size condition gives 2k+2 points. Writing the two level sizes as p=k-r+1 and q=k+r+1 yields feasibility exactly when r^2<=d. The required Hasse-edge count is (k+1)^2-d, so the complement in K_{p,q} has exactly e=d-r^2 edges. The threshold k>=d+1 gives p>e and q>e; hence any such missing-edge pattern is supported on a bounded set of vertices, its ambient isolated complement is canonical, the retained Hasse graph stays connected with no degree-one beat points, and color-preserving isomorphism of the missing graph is exactly order isomorphism for that level orientation. The balanced r=0 case contributes b_d and every r>0 contributes two orientations. Fresh independent enumeration reproduced b_0 through b_5 as 1,1,3,6,16,34 and the resulting stabilized counts 1,3,5,12,30,68. The finite counts corroborate the all-d symbolic argument.

originality.rationale: Originality passes. Barmak--Minian give the foundational all-graph characterization of minimal finite models and, for bouquets of circles, determine the minimum number of points and the necessary edge count; their examples include the three models of the rank-three bouquet and the later book notes uniqueness exactly at square rank. Those structural premises do not enumerate homeomorphism classes in fixed square-deficit families. The audited theorem adds the missing-edge orbit reduction, proves a uniform stabilization threshold, and expresses the stable multiplicity by color-preserving bipartite graph isomorphism counts. Resultary search found no prior formula of this form.
residual_risks: An older enumeration of homeomorphism classes near square ranks could exist outside the terminology of square deficit or missing-edge bipartite graphs, although direct full-text and semantic searches did not locate one.
